简介

（注：英语不是我的母语，所以我使用AI辅助来帮助翻译和润色本教程）

在本教程中，我想展示我当前用于图像生成过程的工作流程。

这不是我一天之内建成的。随着时间的推移，我逐渐开发了它，测试了不同的节点、设置和小的调整，直到找到一个可以在质量、控制和性能之间实现良好平衡的设置。

重要的一点是，我使用的 GPU 相对较弱，仅8 GB 显存。因此，我必须构建一个工作流程，该工作流程仍然可以产生良好的结果，而无需依赖非常笨重的工具或不必要的苛刻方法。

这也是这个工作流程的原因不使用SD 高档。虽然它很有用，但也比较重，而且对于我的硬件来说，它不是最实用的选择。我更喜欢专注于更简单的管道，它更容易运行，并且即使在较低 VRAM 设置上仍然能够产生可靠的结果。

我决定发布2 种变体此工作流程的：

  • 一个基础版本

  • 一个固定版本基本工作流程的一部分，适用于可能对某一特定节点有问题的人

我仍然建议在直接使用文件之前阅读完整的教程，因为了解每个阶段的作用可以更轻松地选择正确的版本并将其适应您自己的设置。

在接下来的部分中，我将逐步完成该过程。

1. 模型、LoRA 设置和指导

第一个块包含工作流程的核心设置：检查站, 的LoRA加载器，以及指导子图.

检查站

检查点通过一个简单的节点加载，并充当整个工作流程的基础模型。

LoRA 设置

在检查站之后，我使用专用的LoRA子图.

我以这种方式构建它的主要原因之一是方便性和可读性。
这个设置让我可以看到：

  • 的LoRA 文件名

  • 的触发词/关键词与 LoRA 相关的

这使得工作流程更易于管理，特别是在使用多个 LoRA 或在不同角色、服装或增强 LoRA 之间切换时。

如图所示，一个例子是我的OC 佑希 LoRA.
在该块中，我可以快速检查文件名、调整 LoRA 强度，还可以在提示中看到正确激活它所需的关键字。

这很有用，因为它可以减少猜测，并且更容易使提示与所使用的 LoRA 保持一致。

此刻，我包括8 个 LoRA 块，这对于我当前的用例来说已经足够了。
当然，这部分是完全可扩展的，所以如果你需要更多的LoRA插槽，你可以毫无困难地扩展它。

当然，如果您只想使用几个 LoRA，只需单击图中显示的第二个图标即可绕过其他 LoRA。

指导子图

该块的最后一部分是指导子图.

在里面，我包括：

  • 动态阈值

  • 略读 CFG

  • 自由大学

此刻，我是不积极使用 FreeU，因为我仍在测试它，而且我还没有找到我认为对我的工作流程完全可靠的值。

另外两个，动态阈值和略读 CFG，更高级，可能更难在简短的教程中清楚地解释。
因此，我不会在这里太深入地探讨他们的技术行为。

我可以说的是，两者都会对最终结果产生显着影响，所以如果你想尝试它们，请小心行事。
我的建议是更改值非常逐渐地，每次仅增加或减少一点，因为即使很小的调整也会在图像中产生明显的差异。

有关此块的更多说明，请随时向 ChatGPT 询问更多详细信息。

2. 基本生成设置

该块包含主要的生成设置：CFG、种子、图像大小、采样器、方向和纵横比。

CFG 值在此处设置，并且由于前一个块的指导设置，我还可以更轻松地使用更高的 CFG 值，有时甚至在 10 左右，具体取决于图像和模型。

对于空的潜在图像大小，我建议从相对较高的基本分辨率开始，就像我的示例一样。这有助于在第一次 KSampler 传递中产生更强的第一个结果，从一开始就具有更好的结构和整体图像质量。

我还在该块中添加了方向和纵横比设置。这些使得从一开始就更容易控制图像的整体取景。根据您的需要，可以手动设置方向，例如纵向或横向，但如果您希望各代之间有更多变化，也可以将其随机化。

对于种子，您可以选择：

  • 如果您想要重复性，请使用固定种子

  • 如果您想要世代之间有更多变化，请使用随机种子

至于采样器，这通常取决于个人喜好。在许多情况下，遵循您在第一个块中选择的检查点的创建者给出的建议也是值得的。


3. 提示和嵌入

这个块非常简单。

在这里你会发现：

  • 一盒用于积极提示

  • 一盒用于负面提示

  • 正极侧有 6 个嵌入槽

  • 负极侧有 6 个嵌入槽

这里没有什么特别复杂的。这只是您构建图像的主要提示结构并添加您想要使用的任何嵌入的部分。

每个嵌入槽都可以根据您的需要绕过（CTRL+B），并且您还可以调整其强度直接在节点中。这为您提供了更多的控制权，而不必每次都重写提示。



4. 第一个 KSampler 通行证

在此块中，您会发现KS采样器我个人更喜欢用于第一遍。

我喜欢这个版本的主要原因是它让我生成图像时实时预览图像，这使得工作流程更易于使用且更易于监控。

另一个有用的细节是这个 KSampler 已经包含了节点内的解码步骤，因此可以直接输出图像，无需事后单独的 VAE Decode 节点。重要的是要确保VAE 连接到 KSampler，在我的工作流程中已经通过无处不在检查点加载程序后面的连接。

对于调度程序，这主要取决于个人喜好。不同的采样器和调度程序的行为不同，因此我建议选择适合您口味的组合，并检查检查点创建者提供的建议（如果可用）。

至于步数，就我而言，我通常需要至少 50 步与我使用的调度程序。也就是说，这不是一个固定的规则。它取决于采样器、调度程序以及您想要的结果类型，因此请随意根据您自己的喜好和工作流程进行调整。

5. 第二次/第一次高档

这是工作流程的第一个高档阶段。

对于这一部分，我使用这个特定的 KSampler 设置，因为它包括脚本输入这让我可以运行潜在高档同时还连接一个高档模型，就像我的例子一样。另一个有用的功能是它还可以加载控制网络模型，这有助于在升级和细化阶段保持图像更加连贯。

我发现这对于更困难的图像尤其有用，例如我想更可靠地保留原始结构的复杂姿势或构图。在这些情况下，ControlNet 可以帮助维护姿势、形状，甚至颜色更加一致。

要正确使用此脚本，右侧的 KSampler应该有：

  • 降噪设置为0

  • 步骤设置为 1

这很重要，因为该阶段的实际设置是在脚本节点，不在 KSampler 本身中。

您通常需要在脚本中调整的主要值是：

  • 去噪

  • 雇用步骤

这些是最直接影响放大结果的最终质量的设置。

当我使用控制网，我经常使用稍高的降噪值，因为 ControlNet 有助于控制图像。但是，您仍然应该小心步骤数，因为较高的值会大大增加生成时间。

对于高档量，我个人不建议超出太多2x。主要原因是生成时间和解码限制。这个KSampler还支持平铺解码，这会有所帮助，但在 2 倍高档以上，您可能会开始看到更多伪像或其他图像问题。

在 KSampler 的右侧，还有一个图像比较器节点，它可以让你比较升级前后的图像，这样你就可以清楚地看到这个阶段发生了什么变化。

还值得一提的是，这脚本节点可能有问题。某些用户无法正确使用它或可能遇到兼容性问题。这正是我创建一个工作流程的第二个版本不依赖于该节点。缺点是，如果没有它，此阶段无法使用 ControlNet.

6.眼部细节师

此步骤致力于改进眼睛，这是最终图像中最重要的焦点之一。

从工作流程的角度来看，这里没有太多解释：该块的目的只是细化眼睛区域并提高清晰度、锐度和整体细节。

与之前的一些高级节点一样，此块包含几个可以显着影响结果的设置。如果您想修改这些值，我建议仔细更改它们并逐步测试它们。

有关此块中的设置的更多详细说明，请随时向 ChatGPT 寻求更多帮助。

7. 第三次 KSampler 通行证

这是第三次 KSampler 传递，尽管在大多数情况下我都会留下它绕过.

与之前的高档阶段相比，没有太多需要解释的地方。此阶段的主要目的是进一步细化微观细节并进一步提高分辨率。在某些图像中，这可以显着改善较小的细节，并使最终结果看起来更加精美。

也就是说，这一步也会使过程明显变慢，所以我不会一直使用它。它对于某些图像可能会有帮助，但如果使用过度，它也会带来新的问题，所以我建议小心使用。

我也此阶段不建议使用ControlNet，因为生成时间变得非常长并且通常不值得。

在这个群里，还有一个自动旁路机制当该组处于活动状态时，稍后会禁用工作流中的另一个节点。正因为如此，重要的是始终绕过整个组本身，而不是仅禁用其中的单个节点。

8. 高档节点

该高档节点仅在以下情况下激活：第三次 KSampler 通道被禁用.

其目的是放大图像并提高结果的整体清晰度。就我而言，我使用RealESRGAN_x4plus_anime_6B，它非常适合动漫风格的图像，通常有助于使图像在放大后看起来更干净、更锐利。

因此，当我决定不使用第三个 KSampler 通道时，此节点充当更简单的最终升级选项。

该模块用于最终的图像抛光和色彩校正阶段。

至此，主要生成过程已经完成，因此本节重点介绍可改善图像最终呈现效果的小型视觉调整。

在此更新版本中，该块包括以下步骤：

  • 图像色彩匹配用于根据参考调整整体颜色关系

  • 奥尔姆图像调整用于对亮度、对比度、伽玛、阴影、中间色调、高光、饱和度、明度和鲜艳度进行精细控制

  • CR 色调用于在需要时应用微妙的色调

  • 图像锐化用于添加最终锐化通道

  • 开始/最终预览节点用于比较校正阶段之前和之后的图像

这部分比前面的阶段更加主观，所以我认为不存在单一正确的价值观。此处使用的设置在很大程度上取决于特定图像以及您想要实现的最终外观。

因此，我建议将此块视为最后的抛光步骤，并根据您自己的喜好调整值。

本节中的预览/比较节点还可以让您在保存最终结果之前更轻松地清楚地评估更改。

10. 保存节点

最后，这是保存节点.

在这里您可以选择：

  • 的文件名

  • 的输出文件夹

  • 的图像格式

  • 的质量设置

  • 的元数据选项

关于元数据，您可以决定是否保存：

  • 的完整的工作流程

  • 只有生成值/参数

  • 或根本没有元数据

所以这个块只是最后的导出阶段，您可以在其中决定如何保存完成的图像。

11. 控制网

这是控制网块，并且它连接到第一遍工作流程的。

这意味着它应该在生成过程的开始，当图像尚未创建时。其目的是从一开始就引导模型走向更具体的姿势或结构。当构图困难并且您想要对初始结果进行更强的控制时，它特别有用。

在此设置中，您最多可以选择3 个预处理器.
大多数时候，我只使用一两个将它们放在一起，所以如果不需要第三个，我只需绕过它。这有助于减少不必要的处理时间，因此如果您不使用预处理器，请确保绕过它。

里面的多ControlNet堆栈节点，您可以控制：

  • 的实力每个 ControlNet 的

  • 当它开始影响一代人时

  • 当它不再影响一代人时

这给了你很大的灵活性。例如，您可以让 ControlNet 在开始时强烈引导图像，然后稍后停止，以便模型在生成的其余时间内拥有更多自由度。

另外，请尝试将您想要实现的姿势与提示本身尽可能匹配，因此请务必仔细编写提示。

只需确保保留开/关开关与您实际使用的预处理器一致。

一个重要的注意事项：在此处所示的示例中，我最终图像没有使用 ControlNet，所以本节仅供参考。您在屏幕截图中看到的设置不是用于教程中显示的生成的设置。

固定版本

我创造了第二个固定版本为可能遇到问题的用户提供工作流程脚本节点在基础版本中使用。

Introduction

(Note: English is not my native language, so I used AI assistance to help translate and polish this tutorial)

In this tutorial, I want to show the workflow I currently use for my image generation process.

This is not something I built in a single day. I developed it gradually over time, testing different nodes, settings, and small adjustments until I found a setup that gave me a good balance between quality, control, and performance.

One important point is that I work with a relatively weak GPU with only8 GB of VRAM. Because of that, I had to build a workflow that could still produce good results without relying on very heavy tools or unnecessarily demanding methods.

That is also why this workflow doesnotuseSD Upscale. While it can be useful, it is also heavier, and with my hardware it is not the most practical choice. I preferred to focus on a simpler pipeline that is easier to run and still capable of producing solid results even on a lower-VRAM setup.

I decided to publish2 variantsof this workflow:

  • abase version

  • afixed versionof the base workflow, for people who may have issues with one specific node

I still recommend reading the full tutorial before using the files directly, because understanding what each stage does makes it much easier to choose the right version and adapt it to your own setup.

In the next sections, I will go through the process step by step.

1. Model, LoRA Setup and Guidance

This first block contains the core setup of the workflow: thecheckpoint, theLoRA loaders, and theguidance subgraph.

Checkpoint

The checkpoint is loaded through a simple node and acts as the base model for the whole workflow.

LoRA Setup

Right after the checkpoint, I use a dedicatedLoRA subgraph.

One of the main reasons I built it this way is convenience and readability.
This setup allows me to see both:

  • theLoRA file name

  • thetrigger words / keywordsassociated with that LoRA

This makes the workflow easier to manage, especially when working with multiple LoRAs or when switching between different characters, outfits, or enhancement LoRAs.

As shown in the image, one example is myOC Yuki LoRA.
In that block, I can quickly check the file name, adjust the LoRA strength, and also see the keywords needed to activate it properly in the prompt.

That is useful because it reduces guesswork and makes it easier to keep the prompt consistent with the LoRA being used.

At the moment, I included8 LoRA blocks, which is enough for my current use case.
Of course, this part is fully expandable, so if you need more LoRA slots, you can extend it without much difficulty.

Of course, if you only want to use a few LoRAs, simply bypass the others by clicking the second icon shown in the image.

Guidance Subgraph

The last part of this block is theguidance subgraph.

Inside it, I included:

  • Dynamic Thresholding

  • Skimmed CFG

  • FreeU

At the moment, I amnot using FreeU actively, because I am still testing it and I have not found values that I consider fully reliable for my workflow yet.

The other two,Dynamic ThresholdingandSkimmed CFG, are more advanced and can be harder to explain clearly in a short tutorial.
Because of that, I will not go too deep into their technical behavior here.

What I can say is that both can have a noticeable impact on the final result, so if you want to experiment with them, do it carefully.
My recommendation is to change the valuesvery gradually, increasing or decreasing them only a little at a time, because even small adjustments can produce visible differences in the image.

For further explanation about this block, feel free to ask ChatGPT for more detailed information.

2. Basic Generation Settings

This block contains the main generation settings: CFG, seed, image size, sampler, orientation, and aspect ratio.

The CFG value is set here, and thanks to the guidance setup from the previous block, I can also work with higher CFG values more comfortably, sometimes even around 10, depending on the image and the model.

For the empty latent image size, I recommend starting with a relatively higher base resolution, like in my example. This helps produce a stronger first result already in the first KSampler pass, with better structure and overall image quality from the start.

I also added orientation and aspect ratio settings in this block. These make it easier to control the overall framing of the image from the beginning. Depending on your needs, the orientation can be set manually, for example portrait or landscape, but it can also be randomized if you want more variation across generations.

For the seed, you can choose either:

  • a fixed seed if you want repeatability

  • a random seed if you want more variation between generations

As for the sampler, that often comes down to personal preference. In many cases, it is also worth following the recommendations given by the creator of the checkpoint you chose in the first block.


3. Prompt and Embeddings

This block is quite straightforward.

Here you will find:

  • one box for thepositive prompt

  • one box for thenegative prompt

  • 6 embedding slots for the positive side

  • 6 embedding slots for the negative side

There is nothing especially complicated here. This is simply the section where you build the main prompt structure of the image and add any embeddings you want to use.

Each embedding slot can be bypassed (CTRL+B) depending on your needs, and you can also adjust itsintensitydirectly in the node. This gives you a bit more control without having to rewrite the prompt every time.



4. First KSampler Pass

In this block, you will find theKSamplerI personally prefer to use for the first pass.

The main reason I like this version is that it lets mepreview the image in real time while it is being generated, which makes the workflow more comfortable to use and easier to monitor.

Another useful detail is that this KSampler already includes adecode step inside the node, so it can output the image directly without needing a separate VAE Decode node afterward. The important thing is to make sure theVAE is connected to the KSampler, which in my workflow is already handled through theAnything Everywhereconnection behind the checkpoint loader.

For thescheduler, this is mostly up to personal preference. Different samplers and schedulers behave differently, so I recommend choosing the combination that fits your taste and also checking the suggestions provided by the creator of the checkpoint when available.

As for thenumber of steps, in my case I usually needat least 50 stepswith the scheduler I use. That said, this is not a fixed rule. It depends on the sampler, the scheduler, and the kind of result you want, so feel free to adjust it based on your own preferences and workflow.

5. Second Pass / First Upscale

This is the first upscale stage of the workflow.

For this part, I use this specific KSampler setup because it includes ascript inputthat allows me to run alatent upscalewhile also connecting anupscaler model, as in my case. Another useful feature is that it can also load aControlNet model, which helps keep the image more coherent during the upscale and refinement stage.

I especially find this useful for more difficult images, such as complex poses or compositions where I want to preserve the original structure more reliably. In those cases, ControlNet can help maintainpose, shapes, and even colorsmore consistently.

To use this script correctly, theKSampler on the rightshould have:

  • denoise set to 0

  • steps set to 1

This is important because the actual settings for this stage are controlled inside thescript node, not in the KSampler itself.

The main values you will usually want to adjust in the script are:

  • denoise

  • hires steps

These are the settings that most directly affect the final quality of the upscaled result.

When I useControlNet, I often work with a slightly higher denoise value, since the ControlNet helps keep the image under control. However, you should still be careful with the number of steps, because higher values can increase generation time quite a lot.

For theupscale amount, I personally would not recommend going much beyond2x. The main reasons are generation time and decoding limitations. This KSampler also supportstiled decode, which can help, but above 2x upscale you may start to see more artifacts or other image problems.

To the right of the KSampler, there is also anImage Comparernode, which lets you compare the image before and after the upscale, so you can clearly see what changed during this stage.

It is also worth mentioning that thisscript node can be problematic. Some users are not able to use it correctly or may run into compatibility issues. That is exactly why I created asecond version of the workflowthat does not rely on this node. The downside is that, without it,ControlNet cannot be used during this stage.

6. Eye Detailer

This step is dedicated to improving theeyes, which are one of the most important focal points in the final image.

There is not much to explain here from a workflow perspective: the purpose of this block is simply to refine the eye area and improve clarity, sharpness, and overall detail.

As with some of the previous advanced nodes, this block includes several settings that can noticeably affect the result. If you want to modify the values, I recommend changing them carefully and testing them gradually.

For more detailed explanations about the settings in this block, feel free to ask ChatGPT for additional help.

7. Third KSampler Pass

This is thethird KSampler pass, although in most cases I leave itbypassed.

There is not much more to explain compared to the previous upscale stage. The main purpose of this pass is to further refinemicro-detailsand increase the resolution even more. In some images, this can noticeably improve smaller details and give the final result a more polished look.

That said, this step also makes the process significantly slower, so I do not use it all the time. It can be helpful for certain images, but it can also introduce new problems if used too aggressively, so I recommend being careful with it.

I alsodo not recommend using ControlNet in this stage, because the generation time becomes extremely long and usually is not worth it.

Inside this group, there is also anautomatic bypass mechanismthat disables another node later in the workflow when this group is active. Because of that, it is important to alwaysbypass the entire group itself, rather than only disabling single nodes inside it.

8. Upscale Node

This upscale node is only activated when thethird KSampler pass is disabled.

Its purpose is to enlarge the image and improve the overall clarity of the result. In my case, I useRealESRGAN_x4plus_anime_6B, which works well for anime-style images and often helps make the image look cleaner and sharper after upscaling.

So this node acts as a simpler final upscale option when I decide not to use the third KSampler pass.

This block is used for the final image polishing and color correction stage.

At this point, the main generation process is already complete, so this section is focused on small visual adjustments that improve the final presentation of the image.

In this updated version, the block includes the following steps:

  • Image Color Matchfor adjusting the overall color relationship based on a reference

  • Olm Image Adjustfor fine control over brightness, contrast, gamma, shadows, midtones, highlights, saturation, value, and vibrance

  • CR Color Tintfor applying a subtle color tint when needed

  • Image Sharpenfor adding a final sharpening pass

  • Start/final preview nodefor comparing the image before and after the correction stage

This part is much more subjective than the previous stages, so I do not think there is a single correct set of values. The settings used here will depend heavily on the specific image and on the final look you want to achieve.

For that reason, I recommend treating this block as a final polishing step and adjusting the values based on your own taste.

The preview / comparison node in this section also makes it easier to clearly evaluate the changes before saving the final result.

10. Save Node

Finally, this is thesave node.

Here you can choose:

  • thefile name

  • theoutput folder

  • theimage format

  • thequality settings

  • themetadata options

Regarding metadata, you can decide whether to save:

  • thefull workflow

  • only thegeneration values / parameters

  • orno metadata at all

So this block is simply the final export stage, where you decide how the finished image will be saved.

11. ControlNet

This is theControlNetblock, and it is connected to thefirst passof the workflow.

That means it should be activated at thebeginning of the generation process, when the image has not been created yet. Its purpose is to guide the model toward a more specific pose or structure from the start. It is especially useful when the composition is difficult and you want stronger control over the initial result.

In this setup, you can choose up to3 preprocessors.
Most of the time, I only useone or twoof them together, so if the third one is not needed, I simplybypass it. This helps reduce unnecessary processing time, so if you are not using a preprocessor, make sure to bypass it.

Inside theMulti-ControlNet Stacknode, you can control:

  • thestrengthof each ControlNet

  • when it starts affecting the generation

  • when it stops affecting the generation

This gives you a lot of flexibility. For example, you can let ControlNet strongly guide the image at the beginning, then stop it later so the model has more freedom during the rest of the generation.

Also, try to match the pose you want to achieve as closely as possible with the prompt itself, so make sure to write the prompt carefully.

Just make sure to keep theOn / Off switchesconsistent with the preprocessors you are actually using.
